summary: This bill removes age restrictions for adults with disabilities to participate in Medicaid buy-in programs, allowing individuals aged 65 and older to be eligible.

scores.thoughts: This bill expands Medicaid eligibility by removing age restrictions for working adults with disabilities, thereby increasing access to public healthcare. This is the central purpose of the bill.
By expanding Medicaid eligibility to more working adults with disabilities, the bill broadens access to a key social safety net program. This directly expands welfare provisions.

The bill expands Medicaid eligibility by removing the under-65 age cap for working adults with disabilities, which will increase federal and state program expenditures. This effect on the deficit is incidental rather than central to a bill whose primary purpose is eligibility reform.

The legislation directly expands government-funded Medicaid coverage to an additional population of working disabled adults, constituting government action to broaden access and lower costs for beneficiaries. This expansion is the core and sole purpose of the bill.
